analysis.session_summary: The window was dominated by broad USD weakness and JPY/CAD strength, with DXY falling 24.0 points (-0.241%) and USD/JPY dropping 51.4 pips (-0.321%). Oil jumped 2.087% to 92.739 on the Iran/Venezuela headlines, but most FX legs had no confident catalyst; only the Bessent stronger-Yen comment showed medium-confidence legs in CHF/JPY and USD/CHF. The risk tape was mixed: SPX fell 37.9 points (-0.491%) while VIX eased 21.0 points (-1.243%), suggesting the USD move was not a simple risk-off bid. No event reaction cleared the measured threshold, so no polarity read is generated.

themes.evidence: DXY/USD fell 24.0 points (-0.241%), USD mean -0.196% against majors; USD/JPY -51.4 pips, USD/CAD -41.9 pips, USD/SEK -423.3 pips.
JPY mean +0.171%, USD/JPY -51.4 pips (-0.321%), CHF/JPY -35.1 pips; Bessent stronger-Yen headline attributed 98% of a 23.4-pip CHF/JPY leg.
Brent/USD +189.6 pips ($0.01) to 92.739, +2.087%; headlines on US strike on Iran's Larak Island and Venezuela oil deal.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD carved a shallow -10.3-pip dip from 19:00 to 23:45 and then a +39.6-pip recovery to close at 1.16165 (+29.7 pips), with neither leg showing a confident catalyst according to the measured notes.

scenarios.name: USD rebound on ISM/data strength
scenarios.thesis: The USD is stretched after a broad -0.196% mean drop, and a firm ISM Manufacturing PMI at 16:00 can trigger short-covering; higher ISM Prices would challenge the current USD-negative tape.
scenarios.invalidation: EUR/USD sustains above its 43.9-pip range high and DXY fails to recover from its 99.351 close.

pair_paths.rationale: USD bounce unwinds the 29.7-pip EUR/USD gain; the measured EUR/USD range is 43.9 pips.
Rebound in USD against stretched JPY; USD/JPY range was 72.2 pips after a 51.4-pip drop.
Oil-driven CAD strength may pause if USD recovers; USD/CAD range was 54.0 pips.

scenarios.name: Sustained USD weakness on soft US data and firm EUR CPI
scenarios.thesis: The broad USD decline continues if upcoming data disappoints, while higher EUR CPI supports EUR; the current tape already shows USD mean -0.196% and EUR +0.096%.
triggers: EUR CPI Flash Estimate y/y above 3.3%
scenarios.invalidation: DXY recovers above its 99.351 close and EUR/USD loses the 1.16165 close.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD already +29.7 pips with a 43.9-pip range; firm EUR CPI and soft US data extend the move.
JPY strength +0.171% and USD/JPY -51.4 pips; continued USD softness can push toward the measured 72.2-pip range.
CAD strength +0.15 and oil bid; USD/CAD already -41.9 pips within a 54.0-pip range.

scenarios.name: Geopolitical/oil escalation and risk-off
scenarios.thesis: Brent's +2.087% jump and the Iran/Venezuela headlines could escalate, keeping safe-haven JPY/CHF bid even as equities are fragile; the VIX down -1.243% suggests the market is not paying a classic risk-off premium, making the move more oil-specific.
scenarios.invalidation: No new Iran headline and Brent reverses below its 92.739 close.

pair_paths.rationale: Safe-haven JPY bid; USD/JPY range is 72.2 pips.
CHF safe-haven and current USD/CHF -11.6 pips; range is 29.6 pips.
Risk-sensitive AUD underperforms; AUD/USD range is 18.3 pips.

risks.risk: Oil price spike from Iran/Venezuela headlines
risks.why_it_matters: Brent/USD already +2.087% to 92.739; further spikes can distort USD and inflation expectations and favor CAD/NOK/SEK while hurting risk assets.
risks.watch: Brent/USD, Iran retaliatory headlines, US official comments on Strait of Hormuz.

risks.risk: US ISM Manufacturing PMI/U.S. data disappointment
risks.why_it_matters: DXY already -0.241% and USD mean -0.196%; a soft ISM or JOLTS could accelerate the USD decline and challenge the rebound scenario.
risks.watch: ISM Manufacturing PMI forecast 55.2 vs previous 55.6; ISM Prices forecast 70.5 vs previous 71.1; JOLTS forecast 7.33M vs previous 7.36M.

risks.why_it_matters: Most legs had no clear catalyst, and risk signals are mixed (SPX -0.491% but VIX -1.243%); positioning-driven moves can reverse quickly if headlines shift.
risks.watch: DXY close near 99.351 and USD/JPY close near 159.68.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: The next catalyst is the 11:00 EUR CPI flash estimate (forecast 3.3% y/y vs 2.9% previous) followed by the 16:00 US ISM Manufacturing PMI (forecast 55.2 vs 55.6) and JOLTS (forecast 7.33M vs 7.36M). These can confirm or reverse the broad USD weakness; a hot EUR CPI and soft ISM would extend the current EUR/USD and USD/JPY trends.
